title: Emperor Penguins Survive -43°C by Doing the Wave

scenes.text: Penguins survive minus 43 degrees by doing the wave.
Thousands pack together, up to 21 birds on every square meter. So tight that nobody can really move.
Yet the whole huddle creeps forward. Every 30 to 60 seconds, each penguin shuffles a few inches, row after row.
Scientists filmed it with time-lapse cameras for four hours and watched the wave roll through the crowd.
The steps keep the huddle packed, move it along, and reorganize it without disturbing the birds in the middle.
Inside a huddle the air can reach about 37 degrees Celsius. Outside it, minus 43. Now watch it again.

subject: emperor penguin
description:
Emperor penguins survive minus 43 degrees Celsius by moving together in a slow wave.
Packed up to 21 birds per square meter, each one takes a tiny step every 30 to 60 seconds, which keeps the huddle tight and moving.
Have you ever seen a penguin huddle on video?
first_comment: Penguins in the middle of a huddle can reach 37 degrees Celsius while it's minus 43 outside. Would you take the middle or the edge?
